blocks.text: Connecting With Ourselves, Each Other, and The Earth
Check out our *NEW* programs!
Screen-free time in nature. Programs for people of all ages.
Spark Your Child's Connection to Themselves, Each Other, and the Earth!
Wayfinders Base Camp ignites a love for nature and fosters social-emotional learning through:
Weekly Fire Circles & Nature Games: Deepen connections with the outdoors and each other through engaging activities.
Social-Emotional Learning & Leadership Development: Build confidence, communication skills, and empathy in a supportive environment.
Community Building: Create lasting friendships and a sense of belonging within a caring group.
Flexible Scheduling & Growth for All Ages:
Choose Your Day: Weekly after-school sessions on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays or (or pick two or all three days for a 10% discount).

Same-Age & Mixed-Age Groups: Cater to individual preferences while fostering mentorship and village building. In mixed-age groups, younger children find role models in older kids, while older ones develop leadership skills by mentoring their peers.
What is Wayfinders?

We are living at a time when we are increasingly disconnected with ourselves, each other, and the earth. Wayfinders offers a solution: Mindfulness, community building, and nature immersion. Through social emotional learning and sustainability practices, Wayfinders provides experiential opportunities to disconnect (from technology) and reconnect with ourselves, each other, and the earth.

Wayfinders creates a fun & safe space to build interconnectedness through nature guided experiences and social & emotional mentoring. The program explores leadership development and community building, and offers Junior Mentor or Mentor-in-Training programs; and for those interested - Rites of Passage.
Wayfinders experiential opportunities with nature connection and social emotional learning result in positive impacts including:
shaping future sustainability advocates
addressing mental health challenges
increasing opportunities for diverse and underserved participants.

Why Wayfinders?

Why did climate activist - Gwen Merkin, and School Counselor - Leah Gozhansky create Wayfinders on the Hudson? After 30 years of combined experience, the evidence of a need for this program is very clear! Click on the below sections to learn more about the call to action.

Core Values Participants are encouraged to see themselves as part of the web of lifePractice gratitude, land acknowledgement, and sit spot Explore self-awareness Build relationships and community Connect with the earth Become more mindful of where things come from and where things goCultivate leadership skills Be called to social action

Leadership Development Identifying the challenges that our world and communities face is the easy part. Learning how to take steps to address issues like climate change and structural racism takes grit and guts. Developing small and measurable group goals, we learn to move from identifying a problem to forming and implementing a solution. Wayfinders participants bring these skills to their communities to make a larger impact.

Community Building & Social Justice How do we create the community we want to be part of? The Wayfinders community is a microcosm of our larger community and a playground for defining the values that we want to live by. Exploring how our family and personal values align (or don’t align) with the kind of community we want to live in helps participants find their way to taking the steps to transform their communities.We look at our community with fresh eyes, trying to understand the systems and structures all around us that have led to profound inequality. And we consider organizing and leadership opportunities to overcome these barriers.

Adolescence to Adulthood The adolescent stage is where the term “identity crisis” originated. Adolescents stop looking to their parents/guardians for guidance and instead look toward their peers and other adults. The “social brain” activates as they start orienting towards the bigger world. Individuation is front and center during this developmental time. Wayfinders are surrounded by skilled mentors and a supportive peer group, where genuine and positive identities have a chance to evolve. Participants at Wayfinders will find relevance and meaning through self-driven experiences and project based learning.

Safe Space, Belonging Humans are social beings, wired for membership in a group. When children are consumed by monitoring their environment for cues of rejection, they can’t take in new information. Social media is a cesspool for rejection - kids feel left out when they see gatherings that they are not included in and are subjected to constant comparison as they scroll through their feeds. This onslaught of rejection impacts self-confidence and creates vulnerability to mental illness.Wayfinders are encouraged to be their most authentic selves as they explore the big questions of who they are, how they relate to people, and what they want to contribute to the world. Participants will thrive in a culture of kindness, where they feel safe and a sense of belonging.

Technology, Social Media, COVID, the Climate Crisis Our children spend more time indoors and on screens and are more isolated than they have ever been. Children spend 3-7 hours a day on screens and miss out on childhood experiences necessary for healthy development. Depression, anxiety, and suicide rates are on the rise and scientific evidence makes it clear that there are long-tem detrimental impacts on the brain. The climate crisis is real, and our kids (and all of us) are unclear about the inevitable shifts. Children today may need a different skill set to succeed in the new world than those that we were prepared for. The scientific evidence is clear- spending time outdoors, in nature, improves overall mental health. Therapists are prescribing time in nature rather than medication. Wayfinders gather in the woods and spend time bonding and sharing around fire circles where we slow down and feel the beauty of connecting with ourselves, each other, and the natural world. We practice survival skills that build our relationship with the elements as we explore animal tracking, shelter and fire building, plant, tree, and mushroom identification, and earth crafts.

Your Child’s Future Transformative experiences during this stage of life, sets the stage for the future. EQ (Emotional Quotient) is now understood as a better indicator of success than IQ (Intelligence Quotient) and is used to identify leaders, good team players, and people who work well independently.Wayfinders experiences sharpen EQ through social emotional learning, team building, nature connection, leadership development, and exercise. Wayfinders infuses soft and hard skills necessary to help navigate the social world and increase resilience. Learning to self-monitor and regulate emotions will have positive lifelong impacts.

Rites of Passage In today’s busy world, we find that we are often rushing from one activity to the next. In this scenario, life starts to feel like a run on sentence, without punctuation or time for breath. Between school, extracurriculars, busy weekends, and non-stop technology, we are running ragged and often failing to pause for reflection, celebration, or re-calibration.Rites of passage serve as a way of pausing and honoring significant milestones as we transition from one stage into another. Ceremonies allow us to hold space for these moments and make them stand out as special, beautiful, meaningful, and memorable. Wayfinders experience rites of passage in group and individual ceremonies and recognize the significance of their personal growth and their impact on the larger community.
Our children are disconnecting from themselves, their families, communities, and the earth as they enter their teenage years.
Wayfinders carves out time for youth to step away from the daily, to connect with purpose.
Land Acknowledgment and Responsibility

The Wayfinders team recognizes that the land where we live, work and play exists within the territory of the Lenape. We acknowledge the Lenape for their enduring stewardship of this place throughout the centuries and still today. We recognize a responsibility to learn about this history while educating new generations about how to live in right relationship with the earth and all of her inhabitants. Learning and relationship building is an ongoing pursuit and we welcome guidance and feedback from all as we endeavor to repair and restore this relationship.

blocks.text: Mentor Positions!
We are looking for Mentors to support our Nature Connection Programs (Base Camp) for 2nd-8th graders. Learn more about Wayfinders here!
Please apply here and email your resume or CV to: wayfindersonthehudson@gmail.com.
Mentors-in-Training Internship!
We are looking for Mentors-in-Training to participate in our Nature-Guided Youth Mentor Program (Base Camp) for 2nd-8th graders. Learn more about our program here!
Please apply here. If you’d like, you can also email your CV to: wayfindersonthehudson@gmail.com.

About the Program Wayfinders on the Hudson provides nature-based, social-emotional learning opportunities for children and youth. The programs focus on nature connection, community building, social action, and coming of age. Our program is open to all youth ages 2nd-12th grade.

At Wayfinders on the Hudson, we integrate nature-based, collaborative, interdisciplinary project-based learning (PBL) and thoughtful self-reflection with high quality mentoring. Our mission is to support youth in their evolution as they grow from a child into a teenager by instilling nature connection, interdependence, confidence, leadership skills, and self-awareness, ultimately resulting in designing and building a life in which they thrive, and have the skills to engage in repairing the world.

Our Team The most important part of any job is who you’re working with. Wayfinders on the Hudson is a startup program. Our team is FUN, eco-centric, integral, innovative and collaborative. We take risks and sometimes they flop, but we find ourselves constantly learning, and improving upon who we are and what we deliver, and our passion for bringing this program to life takes us into the unknowns with joy.
What Sets Wayfinders on the Hudson Apart?
We are working on building a village and cultural repair
We explore earth connection & survival skills
Relationships & gratitude are central to our approach
Youth can experience rites of passage with our program

blocks.text: Corporate Retreats
Get outside and become the best company you can be

Tune in to your senses When you sit at a desk and only communicate via video conferences and calls, your innate skills at reading body language and being part of an interconnected community, can atrophy. Wayfinders begins with tuning back in.

Tune into the seasons Work ebbs and flows just like the seasons change. When we syncopate our rhythms with nature, we harness the power to become more grounded, pace ourselves, connect with our purpose, and find out that sometimes slowing down can actually make us more productive.

Meet your team in a new way Being outside and playing with your colleagues brings you together in ways that do not happen inside four walls of a conference room. Your true nature is revealed and you see each other through new angles that support your engagement at work.
Get to know your colleagues in a whole new light!
Quote from Jordan Zelniker, CIO, Econoco Corporation on Wayfinders Corporate Retreats
“We are still feeling the good vibes from Monday! Even though it didn’t feel like a Monday! Hahaha.
Thank you again for putting together such an impactful experience for our team. It really set the stage for a very productive 2-day planning session. We got A LOT done!
Really appreciate all you did.”

blocks.text: Diversity, Equity, Inclusion
Purpose

Diversity, equity, and inclusion are essential for Wayfinders to achieve its mission. A commitment to DEI is a deeply held value, but it is also a practical necessity for the organization to achieve its objectives. In addition to an explicit expression of our values, DEI means taking concrete action, and holding ourselves accountable to meaningful outcomes.
Values
Racism is often structural in nature, embedded in systems, policy, our physical environment, and our unconscious behaviors and psychology.
Structural racism explains profound and persistent inequality in our everyday lives.
DEI includes race, ethnicity, nationality, class, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, and disability.
DEI, and dismantling structural racism, is central to our program, but it also guides our internal operations and organizational culture.
Action
DEI is an explicit element of Wayfinders’ mission statement.
Wayfinders operates regionally, prioritizing long-term, trust-based relationship building in communities of color and additional marginalized communities.
Substantial resources are allocated to recruitment and retention of program participants, staff, and lay leaders in communities of color and additional marginalized communities.
Governance, advisory, and decision-making structures reflect regional diversity.
Program design always incorporates DEI.
Wayfinders’ compensation policy and financial investment decisions will conform to this DEI policy.
Wayfinders is a learning organization. Substantial resources are allocated to regular and ongoing DEI training, monitoring, assessment, and reporting involving the entire organization.
Accountability
Wayfinders ensures safe and effective ways for internal and external concerns related to DEI to be reported.
Wayfinders regularly reports its performance relative to these principles and action steps.
This policy is easily accessed, and maintained and adjusted as necessary according to Wayfinders’ governance protocols.

blocks.text: Frequently asked questions.

My child has conflicts with other extracurricular activities at times, can he or she still participate in Wayfinders? You are not alone! We are getting this feedback from a lot of families, and the struggle is real.We hope that kids participating in ongoing weekend activities may elect to skip (for part or the entire activity) once a month without significant repercussions. While we believe that the best way to participate in Wayfinders and get the most out of our program is to attend in its entirety, we understand that your child may have to miss occasionally due to other commitments.Bottom line, it is our strong belief, (and obviously we are biased!) above all else in these times, our kids need time to unplug to recharge and reconnect, and the best way to do that is with friends in nature. We think this is worth prioritizing.

Where do the retreats and fire circles take place? Retreats and weekly fire circles take place at Lenoir Nature Preserve, on the boarder of Hastings and Yonkers. The location has an indoor space for severe weather days.

Why are service projects included in the program? Actively participating in creating healthier and more sustainable communities is one of the pillars of the Wayfinders experience. We support participants with exploring the building blocks necessary for affecting change. Exposure to the step-by-step process in planning and implementing a service project will initiate Wayfinders as leaders in their communities.

Are the fire circles and retreats multi-age groups or will you be dividing up the groups by age? The retreats/fire circles will begin as a same-age groups, but following opening circle & gratitude, we will often split into multi age-based or interest-based groups, depending on the activity. Sometimes we will partner older and younger participants to create a peer mentoring component to the program. At the end of the retreats/fire circles - we will regroup to reflect as a same age group in our closing circle.

I am interested in a clearer understanding of who this program is and isn't ideal for. Wayfinders is ideal for kids and families interested in building stronger communities, developing leaders, and connecting with nature, and are willing to step off of the treadmill (even if just for an afternoon) to explore the quiet and stillness of being away from technology, rushing from one activity to another, and the pressures of daily life, to observe, reflect, and learn in community and in nature. It is not ideal for kids who are unwilling to get dressed in layers and be outside (although we have witnessed kids (and adults) who did not think they would enjoy this, find themselves enjoying deeply and surprising themselves once in the mix.)

What are the details about the specific content of the courses, and more specific details about the range of topics that will be covered? Programs are in the woods!We will start with opening circle and gratitude and end with closing circle and reflections. By sharing the “story of the day” or the themes or moments that stuck with kids during the program, they further expand their understanding of what they learned. Programs include development of leadership skills (every participant will be encouraged to participate as a leader during the program and will be mentored on how to authentically bring themselves into the program).Nature games and physical challenges will be included in our programs.We will work with our hands with natural materials (for example - wildcrafting or foraging, making bowls or spoons from logs, cordage, dream catchers, fire building/tending, knife skills, shelter building, etc.)We will integrate creative arts like music (i.e. drumming, singing), and arts (i.e. crafting with nature, mandalas), movement (i.e. choreography) into our work.Programs inspire community building both within our immediate Wayfinders community, and beyond as participants take on issues in our community (i.e. lobbying for banning of leaf blowers, and idyling)Activities will be designed to help youth discover and communicate their natural gifts and passions. We believe strongly that if kids start with their natural talents and then engage in activities that give them the experience to pursue their passions, that the path to self-discovery will be a rewarding and meaningful one. Stay tuned for our curriculum page with more details!

What will my kid(s) take away from the Wayfinders Experience? A stronger connection with nature.A broader understanding and feeling of interconnection with themselves, each other, and the earth.Leadership skillsA strong connection to the Wayfinders Community and the community at large.Exploration and identification of personal passions.Survival skills (shelter, fire, plant identification, animal tracking, etc.)The drive and skills to take action on local and global issues.

What happens when my kid(s) complete the Wayfinders Base Camp program? Upon completion of the program, participants and their families are invited to be part of a coming of age rite-of-passage experience. Additionally, participants are invited to apply to be a peer mentor. Your child will step out of the role of participant and into the role of leader and facilitator of the activities. There is no better way to learn the skills than to teach them and there are no better teachers than peers who have been through the program. Your child will learn leadership, problem solving, and mentoring skills, which will also result in a wonderful resume builder.

blocks.text: Rose Blossoms
An invitation to young women ages 12-15 to dive deeply into discovering gratitude, emotional resilience, sacred sisterhood, intuitive knowing, and Earth stewardship.
Limited Spaces and Scholarships Available.

Rose Blossoms is a nature-based rite-of-passage and mentorship program for adolescent girls. Through circle work, outdoor experiences, creative expression, stewardship projects, ritual, and community building, participants develop emotional resilience, deeper self-awareness, connection to the natural world, and supportive relationships with peers and mentors during the transition into young womanhood.

Rose Blossoms will gather seasonally during three weekends over the 2026-2027 school year in order to provide spacious time for deepening connections with ourselves, each other, and the earth, and the Rose Blossoms themes.

Between each weekend gathering, a Sunday afternoon family gathering will be held to support the ongoing program and build community within the group. These gatherings will be held on Sunday afternoons from 2-5pm. December 6, March 7, and the girls will be invited for sacred sharing at our seasonal final Base Camp sessions with the greater Wayfinders community.
Parents and caregivers will be supported along the path and given tools to uplift their girls as they step into this process.
Seasonal Gatherings
Three weekend journeys across the 2026–2027 school year with connective gatherings in between to keep the circle strong.
Community & Circle
Small group connection, guided reflection, and supportive mentorship in a safe, welcoming space.
Growth & Stewardship
Hands-on learning, rituals, and Earth stewardship that nourish confidence, compassion, and leadership.
Deep Work, Lasting Impact
Rituals and practices that empower girls to navigate change, trust their inner voice, and step into who they are becoming.
Rose Blossoms will:
• Discover their own purpose and feeling of belonging.
• Learn and sing songs to support intention and devotion.
• Practice receiving their own songs to share with their communities.
• Learn plants, foraging, and herbalism while strengthening their connection to plant allies.
• Participate in hands-on acts of earth stewardship.
• Enjoy eco-spa experiences and natural beauty practices, products, and gifting.
• Participate in a Grief Circle, Changing Woman Ceremony, Vision Quest, and Rite of Passage.
• Work with emotions through guided reflection, ceremony, and solo time in nature.
Fall Camping Weekend Opening Ceremony

Girls will leave this weekend knowing themselves, each other, and the land so much better than when they arrived. Girls will have an opportunity to create an altar together which will illuminate the path they are on, as they call in support from a larger community. We will sleep under the stars alongside mountain lakes, and dream into the girls they are becoming. Parents/caregivers will be invited to send their daughters off in ceremony as they cross the threshold and begin this work, and invited to stay for a parent track session while the girls are off on their own journey.
DETAILS
October 23-25, 2026
Mountain Lakes Park
Theme: Diving deep into ourselves, our history, our community, our past.
CONNECTIVE OFFERING
A time for girls and their families to stay connected about the important changes underway.
Sunday, December 6th, 2–5pm

Wednesday, December 9th, 3:45–5:45pm (girls only): a time for girls to present something meaningful underway as revealed during the Fall Ceremony—to be witnessed by our greater Wayfinders community (during final Fall Base Camp family gathering).
Winter

As the snow blankets the land, we will cozy up indoors and learn more about ourselves and our changing bodies. We will create and experience natural beauty care for ourselves and to gift to others on the journey.
January 8-10, 2027
Home in Westchester
Theme: Spa Queens, making, using, and gifting natural beauty products.
Sunday, March 7th, 2–5pm
Spring

Our final weekend together will bring forward all we have learned and experienced together as the girls authorize themselves to become who they are here to be. We will participate in a changing woman ceremony for them to share reflections of each other. Parents and caregivers will be invited to witness the girls as they cross over the threshold again as changed women.
Mountain Lakes or Upstate
Theme: Roses & Rivers: making rose beads/mala necklaces, paddle boarding, river clean up.
A sacred sharing at our final Wayfinders Base Camp Community Gathering.
Wednesday in June TBD: 3:45–5:45: a ceremony to honor the changes in the girls to be witnessed in our greater Wayfinders community (during final Spring Base Camp family gathering).
Roles for Caregivers and Community
Caregivers support track provided for families.
Community members knowledgeable in relevant themes will join our circles.
Youth co-design: participants help plan themes, lead activities, and evaluate the program.
Outcomes and Evaluations
Short-term: improved emotional regulation, stronger peer connections, increased nature engagement & connection.
Medium-term: demonstrated leadership, reduced single-use waste and other sustainability practices.
Evaluation methods: participant reflections, caregiver feedback, facilitator observations, simple ecological metrics for projects.
Sustaining the Community
Create alumni circles for older youth to mentor newer cohorts.
Document activities and outcomes to support funding and partnerships.
Maintain seasonal traditions to anchor ongoing identity and belonging.
Rose Blossoms Program Structure

Sessions: 2 seasonal camping trips in fall and spring (Orientation/First Gathering in Fall and Closing/Rite of Passage in Spring), plus Wintertime weekend sleepover, plus connecting gatherings between each weekend journey to keep the changes flowing, and a Summertime expo for the Wayfinders Community to share the learning and growth from the journey.
Group size: 12 participants to balance intimacy and diversity of perspectives.
Facilitators: Two trained adults (one lead, one assistant/guide) with experience in youth development, non-violent communication, outdoor education, girls rite of passage.
Session Rhythm: welcome circle → check-in → thematic exploration and/or skill practice → small-group project or reflection → closing ritual.
General Gathering Themes
Belonging — identity mapping, group agreements, trust-building activities.
Body & Mind — mindfulness, healthy boundaries, stress tools, moon cycles and synching.
Relationships — active listening, conflict resolution, consent education, non-violent communication.
Place — nature walks/hikes, local ecology, seasonal cycles.
Action — low-waste swaps, service projects, planting, clean ups, gifting.
Leadership & Celebration — project presentations, peer recognition, transition rituals.
Activities & Practices
Circle check-ins with emotion cards or journaling prompts.
Skill workshops: cooking, foraging, herbalism, self-care and beauty.
Creative projects: earth art, bead making & mala necklaces.
Stewardship actions: native planting, clean ups.
Reflection rituals: gratitude stones, intention-setting, closing songs.
Safety, Inclusion, and Accessibility
Co-created behavioral agreements and consent culture.
Deep mentorship and individualized learning goals.
Low-barrier participation: sliding-scale fees or scholarships; materials provided.
Join the Rose Blossoms Journey

Three immersive camping weekend-long ceremonies and short connective gatherings between the weekends (two Sunday afternoons) across the school year, designed to build self awareness & confidence, resilience, leadership, and lifelong friendships through outdoor adventure and meaningful mentorship. Families are deeply encouraged to join for the full journey for maximum growth, and we understand that may not be the right fit for everyone, so we offer weekend options too.

blocks.text: Contribute to the Wayfinders Scholarship Fund or Apply for a Scholarship below.
Wayfinders Scholarship Policy
Wayfinders believes that tuition should not prevent anyone from joining and participating in our community. However, funding does not yet allow for need-blind admission.

Families who can, are asked to pay full tuition to off-set tuition for families unable to pay the full amount. Wayfinders progressive tuition and scholarship opportunities are a step toward creating equity. This effort relies on our community to uplift each other.

Scholarships draw directly from the Wayfinders Scholarship Fund, which is an ongoing fundraising priority. When these funds are depleted, typically no additional scholarships are available for that program year.

Scholarship applications are processed, and scholarship decisions are made, by a subcommittee of the Wayfinders Board of Directors. The members of this committee are responsible for executing the scholarship process according to the mission and values of the organization, with integrity and impartiality.
There are limited opportunities for families to provide in-kind donations of goods or services to help offset tuition, depending on organizational needs at a given time.

Families seeking scholarships can apply directly through the registration form, and may select from a range of options. A Scholarship Committee member may follow up with the family directly with any additional questions, and request documentation of free and reduced lunch designation.
In addition to scholarships, transportation assistance is available through our parent coordinated program which connects those in need of rides with other participants.
Snacks are available at programs.

blocks.text: School Programs
Professional Development Wayfinders provides facilitation workshops for teachers to integrate the practices of nature connection and social emotional learning into curriculum and advisory.

Early Childhood Our Early Childhood experience provides a rich sensory connection with the natural world that serves as joyful building blocks as children grow into their relationships with the natural world.
Student Community Building Wayfinders provides opportunities to cultivate community among new and existing students through facilitated nature connection and team building activities.

Sustainability Field Trips & Retreats From pollinator plants to team building, Wayfinders field trips & retreats get students and teachers connected & curious about nature! Customized half, whole day or camping trips.
School Programs

Wayfinders provides direct service to schools through Professional Development, School-Day Programming (Specials), Extended Day/Enrichment (After School), Field Trips, Clubs, Lunch time Enrichment, Family Circles, and Caregiver & Me.

Our seasonally based, year-long curriculum ensures that our youth connect with nature and their community around them, and build a bond that encourages them to protect the earth throughout their lives.
The Wayfinders experience provides rich sensory connections with the natural world that serve as a joyful building block as children grow into their relationship with nature.
Professional Development Transform your team’s outlook & expertise on integrating nature connection into curriculum
Begin to instill a personal connection with the natural world, which translates into wonder and curiosity, that is contagious with students
Learn about your school’s surrounding ecosystem
Discover how to bring the outdoors inside your classrooms
Build community and connection among your faculty
School Day Specials Wayfinders will join your community during the school day on a monthly, quarterly, bi-annual, or annual basis to provide seasonal, nature connection & SEL programming
Programs run through the grades with age-based curriculum
Customization opportunities are available
Support staff must be present and engaged
Extended Day Supplement and differentiate your program by offering Wayfinders nature connection as part of your “lunch bunch” or after school enrichment program throughout the school year
Field Trips Customized experiences based on curricular interests focused on nature, SEL, and seasonally-based themes
Trips can be as close as in the woods outside of your school or at one of our many outdoor locations

Family Circles Wayfinders builds community through facilitated programs for school families on a monthly, quarterly, bi-annual, or annual basis to provide seasonal, nature connection & SEL programming.

Option 1: Facilitated parent/caregiver groups happen in tandem with children’s programming so parents/caregivers can catch their breath while connecting more deeply with others in their new community, and exploring parent/caregiver & community issues. Children engage in a nature connection/SEL activity during parent/caregiver groups.

Option 2: Facilitated parent/caregiver groups offer the option for parents/caregivers to connect alongside their children in nature. These experiences will help create the foundation for a long term family connection in and with nature.

Caregiver & Me Wayfinders supports building community for new parents through weekly facilitated meet-ups where new parents/guardians/caregivers bond while their babies (under 2 years old) experience sensory play in nature to build their relationship with nature.
Wayfinders Work with Schools: Community Building & Faculty Training

One-on-one activities like pair shares This game of “Shapeshifter” got teachers and administrators to hone their observation schools in preparation for supporting advisees through the Advisory Program.

Contemplative activities like "sit spot" and journaling Sit spot provides an opportunity to find a quiet place to observe nature with all of your senses. This opportunity to clear your mind often results in a sense of peace and connection with the natural world.

Inside schools building culture We love being outside and in nature and we also realize that a lot of time is spent inside the four walls of classrooms in schools. We join forces with teachers to bring nature into the classroom, especially when outdoor conditions don’t allow us to be outside.

Outside in City parks or on your school grounds Nature is everywhere, even in the City, and we work with schools to find space to connect with nature. If you are fortunate enough to have access to nature on your schools grounds, we will come to you and help you learn about the local flora and fauna that live outside your door.
Wayfinders Work with
Bard High School Early College (BHSEC)- Bronx

Wayfinders partners with Bard High School Early College and their new campus in the Bronx. Through this partnership we provide professional development for the faculty to support teachers who also serve as advisors.

Wayfinders provides teachers with direct experiences with social emotional learning in preparation and support for the work they are required to do to support students in underserved communities in the Bronx. blocks.text: Wayfinders for schools
School Programs

Wayfinders provides direct service to schools through Professional Development, School-Day Programming (Specials), Extended Day/Enrichment (After School), Field Trips, Clubs, Lunch time Enrichment, Family Circles, and Caregiver & Me.

Our seasonally based, year-long curriculum ensures that our youth connect with nature and their community around them, and build a bond that encourages them to protect the earth throughout their lives.
The Wayfinders experience provides rich sensory connections with the natural world that serve as a joyful building block as children grow into their relationship with nature.
Ways we work with schools
Professional Development
Transform your team’s outlook & expertise on integrating nature connection into curriculum
Begin to instill a personal connection with the natural world, which translates into wonder and curiosity, that is contagious with students
Learn about your school’s surrounding ecosystem
Discover how to bring the outdoors inside your classrooms
Build community and connection among your faculty
School Day Specials
Wayfinders will join your community during the school day on a monthly, quarterly, bi-annual, or annual basis to provide seasonal, nature connection & SEL programming
Programs run through the grades with age-based curriculum
Customization opportunities are available
Support staff must be present and engaged
Extended Day
Supplement and differentiate your program by offering Wayfinders nature connection as part of your “lunch bunch” or after school enrichment program throughout the school year
Field Trips
Customized experiences based on curricular interests focused on nature, SEL, and seasonally-based themes
Trips can be as close as in the woods outside of your school or at one of our many outdoor locations
Family Circles
Wayfinders builds community through facilitated programs for school families on a monthly, quarterly, bi-annual, or annual basis to provide seasonal, nature connection & SEL programming.

Option 1: Facilitated parent/caregiver groups happen in tandem with children’s programming so parents/caregivers can catch their breath while connecting more deeply with others in their new community, and exploring parent/caregiver & community issues. Children engage in a nature connection/SEL activity during parent/caregiver groups.

Option 2: Facilitated parent/caregiver groups offer the option for parents/caregivers to connect alongside their children in nature. These experiences will help create the foundation for a long term family connection in and with nature.
Caregiver & Me

Wayfinders supports building community for new parents through weekly facilitated meet-ups where new parents/guardians/caregivers bond while their babies (under 2 years old) experience sensory play in nature to build their relationship with nature.
Community Building & Faculty Training
One-on-one activities like pair shares
This game of “Shapeshifter” got teachers and administrators to hone their observation schools in preparation for supporting advisees through the Advisory Program.
Contemplative activities like "sit spot" and journaling

Sit spot provides an opportunity to find a quiet place to observe nature with all of your senses. This opportunity to clear your mind often results in a sense of peace and connection with the natural world.
Inside schools building culture

We love being outside and in nature and we also realize that a lot of time is spent inside the four walls of classrooms in schools. We join forces with teachers to bring nature into the classroom, especially when outdoor conditions don’t allow us to be outside.
Outside in City parks or on your school grounds

Nature is everywhere, even in the City, and we work with schools to find space to connect with nature. If you are fortunate enough to have access to nature on your schools grounds, we will come to you and help you learn about the local flora and fauna that live outside your door.

Our Story

Gwen (Nature Connection Specialist & Trained Eco-Psychologist) & Leah (School Counselor & Certified Nature Informed Therapist) have been in each others lives for more than fifteen years and have been working together at Wayfinders for the last five! Their synergies are truly magical and together they elevate all things eco, psychology, and mentoring into a collaborative dynamic duo full of intense joyfulness and smarts. They have successfully run programs for all ages, from newborns through elders together. Wayfinders is their platform to harness sunshine and smiles, and manifest social and environmental change.

The fusion of Gwen's nature connection & Leah's counseling and coaching creates a powerful combination. Additional support is provided by our stellar team of seasoned nature connection mentors and board members.

Gwen Merkin
Co-Founder, Executive Director
MA City Planning, LEED AP, Wild Earth Teacher Training, Certificate in Ecopsychology

Gwen is a climate and cultural repair activist. In addition to Wayfinders, Gwen consults with individuals and families working to reduce their carbon footprint, and to inspire and transform neighborhoods and communities. She spent 11 years managing Corporate Sustainability and ESG programs at Underwriters Laboratories (UL) working with REITs on strategic sustainability and culture change. She worked at Cushman & Wakefield as a Sustainability Strategist, Steven Winter Associates as a Sustainability Consultant, and at the New York City Department of City Planning in Environmental Review. Gwen's experience completing the Wild Earth Apprenticeship & Teacher Training - an in-depth experiential training on nature mentoring, wilderness living skills, & creating connective nature experiences - motivated her to fulfill her long-standing dream of developing Wayfinders. Gwen was Chair of the Aligned Center Mentorship Program, life cycles teacher at Slide Ranch, K-12 curriculum developer for the Service-Learning Waste Management Program, Training Director for Amigos volunteers in community organizing & Spanish, conference and protest organizer for the Native Forest Network, City Repair community organizer in Portland, OR, and developer and teacher of a UVM course on Ecopsychology. She completed her BA in Environmental Studies and Sociology from UVM and received her MA in Urban and Region Planning from PSU. Gwen strongly believes in Wayfinders mission to provide youth with the tools to prepare for and become leaders of their generation.
Source profile: /gwen
Leah Gozhansky
Co-Founder, Program Director
M.A Psychological Counseling, Ed.M Psychological Counseling & Education, Certified Nature Informed Therapist

Leah is a Certified Nature-Informed Therapist who spent fifteen years working As a School Counselor at Ardsley High School and Bard High School Early College in Manhattan. She taught elementary school through Teach for America. Her extensive experience working in schools is complemented by her work in a psychiatric hospital and substance abuse clinic. She currently works as the Program Director of Wayfinders & facilitates walk and talk counseling sessions in the woods with adults. Leah earned her Masters degrees in Psychological Counseling from Columbia University and a Masters of Education through National Louis University, and a BA in Psychology from the University of Vermont. Leah is certified in Dialectical Behavior Therapy (Step A) and Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction, and has received foundational training in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy. She is certified in child and adolescent yoga. Leah believes deeply in the mental health benefits of nature connection. She brings a wealth of experience in social-emotional learning, counseling, mindfulness, meditation, reflection, validation, group dynamics, and interpersonal relationships to foster a strong sense of self and a deeper connection to our community and the world around us.
Source profile: /leah
Sayako Aizeki-Nevins
Mentor
Sayako is a Wayfinders Mentor who works with youth in Base Camp and early childhood educators in Wayfinders’ teacher trainings.

Sayako recently graduated from Mount Holyoke College with a degree in Geography and Economics. Her studies focused on human-environment relations and currently inform her interest in fostering meaningful connections between people and the environment. Sayako also brings her experiences from climate justice organizing spaces and her training as a Junior Master in Taekwondo to Wayfinders’ dynamic community.
She looks forward to learning with and from everyone at Wayfinders!
Source profile: /sayako-aizeki-nevins
Rebecca D’Elia
MA Psychological Counseling, School Counselor, NOLS Instructor

Rebecca is Wayfinders Lead Mentor and oversees all of Base Camp. She is an experienced outdoor educator and trained school counselor. She is passionate about helping people gain confidence in themselves and connect with one another through outdoor experiential learning. She spent six years teaching and leading at the High Mountain Institute in Colorado, where she filled many roles, including French Teacher, Environmental Ethics Teacher, Wilderness Instructor, Student Advisor, and Dean of Students. She is a trained National Outdoor Leadership Instructor, and she has run pre-teen and teen empowerment programs such as Girls on the Run and Smart-Girl. Rebecca earned her Masters of Education in Psychological Counseling from Columbia University, and her BA in Education and French at Colby College. She has been leading young people in the woods for over 15 years and plans to do so for as long as she is able!
Source profile: /rebecca-dellia
Bryte Gordon
Research Scientist, Ph.D.

Bryte Gordon is a Ph.D. research scientist who studied small molecule metal enzyme mimics and specialized in x-ray crystallography. For over 15 years she has been working in the realm of intellectual property law with cutting edge innovators in biotech and green tech. Through it all, Bryte remains a child at heart and her deepest love is to be in the woods with little people.

As a graduate student, Bryte was a founding member of Women in Science at Columbia, where she helped run the Saturday Science Starters program that hosted young girls from Harlem at the Columbia Chemistry Department to engage in fun and enriching science experiments.

Bryte has also been an active member of the Non-Violent Communication community for a number of years now and is excited to continue to cultivate opportunities for deep listening, empathic connection and awareness with nature, within herself, with the Wayfinders tribe and beyond!
Source profile: /bryte-gordon
Sonjaia McCrae
Sonjaia has an exceptional amount of experience working with children from being a camp counselor at an outdoors-based sleep away camp.

Sonjaia strongly believes that keeping the outdoors instilled in our everyday lives is very important; whether taking a quick walk or sitting outside to take in the environment around you, she prioritizes this herself and wants to bring that quality to children. Sonjaia enjoys taking walks and photographing nature during her free time.
Source profile: /sonjaia-mccrae
Stacie Bartolotta

Stacie brings more than 10 years of nature education experience to the Wayfinders team. For the past 4 years Stacie has been leading nature field trips, camps and partnership programs at Wave Hill Public Garden & Cultural Center. Prior to Wave Hill, Stacie was an Urban Park Ranger for NYC Parks. Valedictorian of her academy class, Stacie led guided camping, canoeing, fishing and survival programs for city residents, Facebook Live programs for thousands across the country and performed wildlife rescues of injured or abandoned animals. Originally from Colorado, Stacie first came to NYC in 2008 for an Americorp program and has never left.

MA in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages, MA Early Childhood Education (in progress), Forest School Educator

Hannah has always had a deep love and appreciation for nature and the youngest learners. She joined the Wayfinders community after working as a first grade teacher in a public, dual-language (Spanish) program in Washington Heights. Hannah was a loved teacher at Little Leaf Forest Preschool over several seasons before having her son.

Prior to teaching in the NYC DOE, Hannah received a M.A. in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages at Teachers College and is currently finishing her M.A. in Early Childhood Education at Bank Street College of Education. She has worked in day care and preschool settings with influences of Reggio Emilia and Montessori.

Hannah is inspired by and committed to the role of the natural world as children’s primary teacher, and cannot wait to see how children’s worlds expand with experiences in the dirt, sun, and forest. Miriam Rubin
B-Mitzvah Guide, Youth Mentor, Interfaith Minister, and the Creative Ritual Director of Wayfinders.

For the past 6 years, Miriam served in the roles of Director of Programming, and Director of Membership at Romemu, NYC’s largest Jewish Renewal community. Miriam has been trained as a Purpose Guide™, Environmental Educator, and Interfaith Minister. Over the past 15 years, she has guided hundreds of youth and adults in deepening their connection to the earth, to their cultural history, and to the wisdom of their soul. Miriam was an outdoor educator for 7 years, where she guided hundreds of students to learn about their relationship with the earth, and designed unique rites of passage programs that supported adolescent development. Miriam is a Nature-based B-Mitzvah guide, she supports each of her students (youth and adults) in gaining their own personal and profound connection to the Hebrew language, to the wisdom of the tradition, and a deeper understanding of their own unique passions and purpose. Miriam sees nature connection, soul-growth, and the involvement of community, as critical practices for creating a meaningful and inspiring response to the urgent times that we're living in. Miriam earned her Bachelors degree at Barnard College in Environmental Science, where she studied the impacts of climate change on the relationship to pollen production in Northeast plant populations. She earned her Massage Therapy License in 2013 and specializes in Somatic Education, trigger-point therapy, and somatic-neural pathway re-education. After being guided through the Soul Purpose Discovery Process under the mentorship of Jonathan Gustin, Miriam found the work to be so profound that she decided to train as a Purpose Guide™. She is proud and humbled to serve as spiritual advisor for Wayfinders on the Hudson as it integrates her life's work.

She partners with nonprofits, foundations, and programs in areas such as strategic thought partnership, program design, learning & improvement, and professional writing.

Jennie has been working to promote quality and equity in the education field for over twenty years, as a nonprofit programmatic leader, professor, researcher, curriculum writer, coach, professional learning facilitator, and middle school teacher. She is also a passionate advocate for mental health agendas and a peer support for struggling parents with Other Parents Like Me.

Jennie comes to Wayfinders as both a professional and a parent with firsthand experience of how nature connection, paired with social-emotional learning and community building, can powerfully support the mental health and identity development of young people.

Jaime Schwarz holds a BA in psychology and philosophy from Colgate University. He served at over a dozen agencies during his copywriting and creative direction career working on over 100 brands. He holds Cannes Lion, Clio, One Show, Webby, and B2B awards and has been published in industry magazines and books. blocks.text: Walk & Talks
We offer nature-informed walk and talk therapy for individuals seeking a therapeutic experience that extends beyond the traditional office setting.

Wayfinders therapists are trained through the Center for Nature-Informed Therapy, we integrate evidence-informed psychotherapy with the restorative qualities of the natural world. Sessions take place outdoors, where movement, fresh air, and connection with the environment can support reflection, emotional processing, and personal growth.
Walk and talk therapy may be especially helpful for those who:
Feel more comfortable talking while moving rather than sitting face-to-face
Experience stress, anxiety, life transitions, grief, or burnout
Seek greater connection with themselves, others, and the natural world
Find that being outdoors helps them feel grounded, present, and open

Nature-informed therapy is not simply therapy that happens outside. It recognizes that our relationship with the natural world can be a meaningful resource in the healing process. Together, we may draw on observations from the environment, seasonal changes, natural metaphors, and mindful engagement with our surroundings to deepen insight and support well-being.

Every session is tailored to your comfort level, therapeutic goals, physical abilities, and the conditions of the day. Whether we are walking, sitting, or pausing along the way, the focus remains on creating a safe, supportive space for exploration and growth.
